Network code that decides whether to cancel a request, tear down a connection, or reroute to another client must treat "no response yet" as ambiguous, not as proof of failure, and must apply its timeout, retry, and classification logic uniformly across every code path that handles the same kind of traffic.

Concretely:
- Before retiring a transport or canceling a pending request on a timeout, probe liveness (e.g. a cheap health-check command) rather than assuming the slow command failed; only act once the probe itself fails or an unrelated reply confirms the socket is actually dead. A single slow write or read should not kill connections that are still making progress.
- When routing a request to "whichever client owns capability X", track real session state (attached vs. explicitly detached), not just socket presence. A client that is still connected but has detached from the session must be skipped in favor of one that is actually attached, and detached-but-connected clients should fail fast rather than hang.
- Any timeout, abort-signal, or proxy-bypass policy you add for a primary request path must also be applied to its fallback path. If the primary call gets a bounded timeout/AbortSignal, the fallback fetch needs the same protection — otherwise the "fast failure" case is handled but the "server drops packets silently" case still hangs indefinitely.
- When classifying endpoints for policy decisions (e.g. "is this local, so skip the proxy and disable idle timeouts"), cover all real-world representations: `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `0.0.0.0` (common for servers bound to all interfaces), and IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms like `::ffff:127.0.0.1`. An incomplete address matcher silently falls back to the wrong policy (e.g. routing a loopback request through a proxy that rejects it) instead of failing loudly.
- Explicit caller-supplied configuration (explicit port, explicit `allowBindFallback`, etc.) must take precedence over any value derived/implied from other inputs; derive defaults only when the caller didn't specify one.

Example of the liveness-probe pattern instead of immediate teardown:
```ts
// Bad: any single command timeout kills the transport
reject(timeoutError);
this.resetFailedTransport(this.socket, timeoutError);

// Good: probe before deciding the connection is actually dead
reject(timeoutError);
const probeOk = await this.healthProbe(); // coalesced, bounded
if (!probeOk) this.resetFailedTransport(this.socket, timeoutError);
```

Add regression tests for the scenarios this protects against: a slow read alongside a healthy pending write, an owner that detaches but stays connected, loopback traffic with `HTTP_PROXY` set and `NO_PROXY` unset, and a fallback network call against a host that drops packets instead of refusing the connection.
